attributes.residual:
THE LAW REFINEMENT, which is the transferable half. v3's PART 3 says to write the early exit as `return`; that is right for the UNFUSED pair and wrong for the fused one, and this function needed BOTH IN THE SAME HELPER. The target's two guards lower differently: at +0x5a4 `fcmpo cr0,f6,f0 / bgt ->5d0` (FUSED, one instruction) and at +0x5a8 `cmpwi r5,30 / bne ->5b4 / b ->5d0` (UNFUSED pair). Writing both exits as `return` gave the unfused pair for BOTH (guard 2 right, guard 1 wrong, O572). Writing both as `goto` to one trailing return gave the fused branch for BOTH (guard 1 right, guard 2 wrong, O570). The spelling is therefore PER-GUARD and the two are independent: `goto <shared trailing return>` fuses, an inlined-callee `return` does not. That also disposes of PART 6(a)'s tail-merge reading here -- the keep has TWO exits returning the same value `fight` (guard 2's `return fight;` and the trailing `done: return fight;`) and pays nothing for it, so the exit COUNT is not what decided this function; the exit SPELLING is.

WHAT REMAINS, and why it is parked rather than open. 28 words, all REGFIELD-ONLY, index-aligned, 0 STRUCTURAL, 0 unpaired -- a pure FPR/GPR recolor. `python tools/gdl/regnorm.py game/enemy/enemy.c damage_enemy` names it as one consistent permutation over the scale block at +0x53c..+0x5d0 (target f1=lbl_80346A30, f2=lbl_80346A28, f3=gCurLevel+172 then the result, f5=threshold then lower, f6=e->health, f4=gCurLevel+188; ours f5, f6, f1, f3, f4, f2 respectively) plus a GPR swap of the two table bases (target `lis r3,@lbl_8011BA10 / lis r4,@lbl_8011B900` then `addi r0,r3 / addi r4,r4`; ours the same instructions with r3 and r4 exchanged) and two later operand EXCHANGES at +0x634 (`fcmpo cr0,f1,f0` vs `fcmpo cr0,f0,f1`) and +0x650. The emission ORDER is identical in both streams, so this is not evaluation order.
